title: Navaratri: nine nights of the Goddess
hookLine: the gods' light becomes the Goddess; nine nights honoring Shakti, God as Mother
carry: shakti: the divine mother is the power in all
last: GOD ACCEPTS WHAT'S OFFERED WITH LOVE.

cards: The gods have lost. Not a skirmish: the whole war. A demon king named Mahisha, who can take the shape of a buffalo, has beaten them, thrown them out of heaven and taken their seats.
They go, humiliated, to Vishnu and Shiva and tell them everything. And as they tell it, something happens that nobody plans. Their anger starts to glow.
That's how the Devi Mahatmya, the great text of the Goddess, opens the battle it's known for.

teach.b: From the faces of Vishnu, Shiva and Brahma, and then from all the gods, a great light pours out, tejas, the text calls it, radiance, and it gathers into one blaze like a mountain on fire.
The blaze takes the form of a woman: the Goddess. Every god gives her something: Shiva a trident, Vishnu a discus, the mountain Himalaya a lion to ride. She laughs, and the sound shakes the worlds.
Then she goes to war with Mahisha. He fights her as a buffalo, then a lion, then a man with a sword, then an elephant, then a buffalo again. She pins him under her foot and ends him.
Behind this story is one of Hinduism's biggest ideas: Shakti. The Goddess isn't a helper the gods made. She is their power, gathered into one, and many Hindus worship God as Mother.
A hymn later in the same text, sung in many homes at Navaratri, praises her as the Goddess who dwells in all beings as power, as mind, as compassion, as mother.
Some teachers read Mahisha, the shape-shifter, as the ego that keeps changing form; that's a reading, not the text.
Navaratri means nine nights: nava, nine, ratri, night. For nine nights in autumn, many Hindus honor the Goddess.
In Gujarat, people dance garba in circles around her lamp until late. In Bengal, it's Durga Puja. In much of the South, families set up golu, steps of dolls.
On the tenth day, Vijayadashami, the day of victory, the good has won.

how: During autumn Navaratri, many Hindus honor the Goddess for nine nights with fasting, recitation of the Devi Mahatmya, garba and dandiya dancing around her lamp in Gujarat, Durga Puja in Bengal, and golu doll displays in the South, ending with Vijayadashami on the tenth day.

o: nine days of fasting before Rama's crowning
nine nights honoring the Goddess in autumn
nine planets honored at a new-moon rite

the demon who takes a buffalo's form

in the Devi Mahatmya their light gathers into one blaze and becomes her.
Mahisha fights only as a buffalo
he becomes a buffalo, a lion, a man with a sword, an elephant, then a buffalo again.
the Goddess is just a helper the gods created
she is their power gathered into one: Shakti, worshiped as the Divine Mother.

games.q: a friend at their first garba asks why everyone dances in a circle around a lamp. what fits today?
o: they're circling the Goddess: the lamp honors her, Shakti, God as Mother.
it's just the easiest shape for a big crowd.
the lamp is there so people can see their steps.
games.why: garba is worship you dance: for nine nights people circle a lamp or image of the Goddess, honoring Shakti.

practice: Sit tall, and say slowly, or just listen inside to, the line many sing at Navaratri: ya devi sarvabhuteshu shakti rupena samsthita. To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as power. Feel your own strength as something given.
If you don't pray, simply name one strength you've been given, and say thank you.

wordCard.voice: Navaratri. Nine nights honoring the Goddess, Shakti, who defeated Mahisha, ending on the tenth day, the day of victory.

orig.note: Sanskrit nava (nine) + rātri (night): the nine nights of the Goddess.

carryVoice: Your line: Shakti, the Divine Mother is the power in all. On the tenth day, victory. See you tomorrow.
